toegepas.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans water or an obstacle 'versper' someone's way; 'pad gestop' reads as a literal translation.
toegepas.fout: 'mense se pad gestop' is a stiff, literal construction; Afrikaans says an obstacle 'versper' someone's way.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The fixed Afrikaans verb reads naturally and the meaning (water blocked people's way) is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: teen die seil en die skip beweeg
toegepas.na: teen die seil, en die skip beweeg
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'en' joins two sentences with their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma before it.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb ('Die wind ... stoot', 'die skip beweeg').
toegepas.rede_keurder: House AWS 2017 rule requires the comma here and nothing else changes.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'vat' is colloquial here; 'beweeg' says the same thing in standard written Afrikaans without echoing 'trek'.
toegepas.fout: 'vat die skip vorentoe' is a loose, colloquial verb for what the force does to the ship.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'beweeg die skip vorentoe' is the plain written verb for the same action, keeps 'Die res van die trek' as subject and avoids repeating 'trek'.

toegepas.voor: lang reise oor die oop see gevaar
toegepas.na: lang reise oor die oop see aangepak
toegepas.rede_vinder: One does not 'vaar' a journey in Afrikaans, and 'gevaar' here can be misread as the noun 'danger'; 'reise aanpak' is idiomatic and grade-appropriate.
toegepas.fout: 'reise ... gevaar' is not a natural collocation and 'gevaar' can be misread as the noun for danger.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'lang reise ... aangepak' is idiomatic, keeps the same people, ship and voyages, and touches no protected wording.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The second verb shares the subject 'Mense', so this is one sentence and AWS 2017 puts no comma before 'of'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The comma separates the two building methods in a sentence that already contains a second 'of' ('bas of vel'), so removing it makes a Grade 4 reader more likely to stumble, and the original is not wrong.

na_skrywer.voor: van boomstompe, bamboes of riet saamgebind
na_skrywer.na: van saamgebinde boomstompe, bamboes of riet
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The trailing participle is awkward word order; the attributive form reads naturally and keeps the meaning.
na_skrywer.fout: The trailing participle 'saamgebind' at the end of the definition reads awkwardly.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This rewords a shared glossary definition beyond a plain spelling or grammar fix, so only the writer may change it for every lesson at once.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.voor: aan 'n mas wat die wind vang
na_skrywer.na: wat aan 'n mas hang en die wind vang
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: As written, 'wat die wind vang' grammatically refers to the mast, not the sail; this matches the study text's own wording and fixes the reference.
na_skrywer.fout: 'aan 'n mas wat die wind vang' lets 'wat' attach to the mast, so the definition can be read as the mast catching the wind.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: A real reference fault, but the fix rewords a shared glossary definition and adds 'hang', so it goes to the writer to fix across lessons.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Hy dra vrag betroubaar, maar hy is stadig.
vlae.rede: 'dra vrag betroubaar' is wooden, but any natural rewording (e.g. 'veilig', 'goed', 'swaar vrag') risks changing what is claimed, so it is left for the reviewer or writer.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: seile wat dun latte styf hou
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: In the Chinese jonk glossary entry this relative clause is ambiguous in Afrikaans: it can be read as sails that hold thin laths taut, the reverse of the intended meaning ('Dun latte hou sy seile styf'). A person may want to reword it, e.g. 'met seile wat deur dun latte styf gehou word'.
